value.first: For a 2-year-old moving from your bed into her own room, I'd use the chair method (parental fading) - not timed crying from another room. She's in a bed now and can just follow you out, so a closed-door wait won't hold; presence you slowly withdraw will. It's trial-tested, the same program a 5-year follow-up found no downside from - just gentler and slower.
value.second: First, set her own safe sleep space and a consistent bedtime (6:30-8:00) with the same 20-30 min wind-down every night: bath, book, bed, feed before the book so eating unhooks from sleep. Then put her down drowsy but awake and sit in a chair right beside her. Calm presence, minimal touch, no feeding or rocking to sleep. Same short goodnight phrase. Treat night wakings the same way.
value.third: Every 3 nights move the chair farther: beside her, mid-room, by the door, hallway in view, then gone - about 2-3 weeks total. Expect protest but less intense than crying it out; consistency is the whole thing. Worth a doctor's look if she snores, gasps, or pauses breathing in sleep - no bedtime method fixes that.
